Based on the provided healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that there is no conclusive evidence to suggest a significant difference in the probability of prenatal diagnosis or termination of pregnancy between fetuses conceived using assisted reproductive techniques (ART) and those conceived naturally. In fact, one study found that ART conception was not significantly associated with the probability of PND (prenatal diagnosis of neonatal death) or TOPFA (termination of pregnancy after failure of first abortion).

However, another study suggested that total prevalence of severe congenital anomalies (severe CHD) would not be adequately assessed if TOPFA are not included. This implies that the presence of a failed abortion could be associated with an increased risk of severe congenital anomalies.

It is essential to note that these findings do not provide clear guidance on whether ART conception or failure of ART should be considered in the context of preterm birth, multiple pregnancy, or recurrent miscarriage. More research and studies are necessary to fully understand the relationship between ART conception, failed abortions, and subsequent pregnancies.
